summary: Tamara Cohen works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2023 under supervisors Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder, having also studied under Joel Tatelman, Bryan Levman, Libbie Mills, and others.

Buddhist studies scholar Tampalawela Dhammaratana studied at Sunethradevi Pirivena, University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, and Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin. He also completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études mentored by Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University, specializing in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served at the University of Delhi (1964–1978), Jawaharlal Nehru University (1978–1994), Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (1994), and the Institute of Chinese Studies.

Tan Poh Beng is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, supervised by Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong (1865–1898) was an active figure in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wang Zhengyi and later under Renshan Yang between approximately 1896 and 1897.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Shuyuan, Chuanshan Academy, and Hunan Normal University, he founded the Sino-Indian Cultural Society and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (1937–1968).
Tanaya Afroz works in linguistics, having studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. Afroz is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar and Fellow at The Asiatic Society.
Tandin Dorji works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held appointments as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College and as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro.

Tanero Sasakawa (1870–1949) was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo from around 1893 to 1896, he held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College attested in 2003.
Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku from around 1797 to 1801 and under Hōdō, and he founded the Kangien academy in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. She has held posts at Harvard University, Maharishi Vedic University, and the Sanskrit Library, where she is attested as Assistant Professor in 2024–2025.

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He taught at the University of Tokyo starting in 1879, joined the Japan Academy in 1885, and became superintendent of Komazawa University in 1891.

Tao Jiang works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and was attested in 2011 as an Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA from Fudan University by 2010 and completed a Magister Artium degree at the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts at Emory University, where she is attested in 2003 as a lecturer and director of the Tibetan Studies Program, and in 2026 as Professor Emerita.
Tarapada Chowdhury (1907–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Edward Hamilton Johnston around 1950. He is attested in 1950 as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College.

Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served at the University of Copenhagen from around 1962 to 1998 and as a curator at the Royal Danish Library from approximately 1962 to 2000.

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University from around 1845 to 1873, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
